approved: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would clarify that references to 'regulations' in two maritime safety Acts generally include Marine Orders made by the Australian Maritime Safety Authority.
It would insert a definition of 'regulations' into the Marine Safety (Domestic Commercial Vessel) National Law Act 2012 and the Navigation Act 2012 to include Marine Orders, with limited exceptions.
The explanatory memorandum states the changes would have no practical impact on maritime industries, as seafarers and vessel owners would continue to comply with existing requirements.
Inserts a definition of 'regulations' into the Marine Safety (Domestic Commercial Vessel) National Law Act 2012 and the Navigation Act 2012 to include Marine Orders.
Sets out limited exceptions to the definition, such as provisions empowering the Governor-General to make regulations or AMSA to make Marine Orders.
Amends two sections of the National Law Act to avoid circular or confusing references to the Law.
Maritime industries, seafarers, vessel owners, and the Australian Maritime Safety Authority.

The Maritime Legislation Amendment Bill 2018 amends the Marine Safety (Domestic Commercial Vessel) National Law Act 2012 and Navigation Act 2012 to clarify that the term 'regulations' includes Marine Orders, ensuring the maritime safety and environmental protection framework operates as intended without practical impact on existing obligations.

The speaker supported the Maritime Legislation Amendment Bill 2018 to clarify marine orders' legal status, but moved an amendment criticising the government for undermining Australian shipping, noting that 12 Australian-flagged vessels had been reflagged under its tenure, and reaffirming the need for a competitive local industry.

The Maritime Legislation Amendment Bill 2018 was commended to the House, amending the Marine Safety (Domestic Commercial Vessel) National Law Act 2012 and the Navigation Act 2012 to define 'regulations' as including marine orders, clarifying that existing obligations for seafarers and vessel owners remain in force with no practical impact on industry.
